briefs.whyMoved: The Russell 2000 rose 46.24 points, or 1.71%, to 2,750.30 on Friday, November 27, after trading between 2,721.39 and 2,751.42. For the week it climbed 168.51 points, or 6.5%, from 2,581.79 on November 20, almost matching the Nasdaq's 6.7%. Friday's gain came as fears about AI stocks eased and all 11 parts of the S&P 500 traded higher, so the buying spread to smaller companies too. Small companies mostly sell inside the US, so a strong economy, like summer growth revised up to 4.3%, helps their profits directly.

watch.what: The job openings report comes out at 10 a.m. ET; fewer openings would point to a cooling job market, which could ease pressure for more rate hikes.
The Fed announces its interest rate decision; traders see a hike as almost certain, so holding rates steady would be a big surprise and a larger hike would be a shock.

briefs.headline: Micron rebounds 7.6% to $646.95 but is still down about 31% in a month
briefs.about: Micron makes memory chips: DRAM, which computers use for short-term memory, and NAND flash for storage. Its chips go into AI data centers, phones and PCs.
briefs.summary: The stock is now 46.69% below its June 25 peak of $1,213.56. CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said on November 18 that 75% of Micron's 2027 supply is already sold and that memory will be even tighter in 2027 and 2028. Micron has 26 long-term customer deals backed by $32 billion of upfront cash and promises. It ended its last year with $73.5 billion in cash versus $5.2 billion of debt.
bull: For the quarter ending in November, Micron guided sales of $61.5 billion and profit of $38.15 per share, which it expects to be the low point for margins this year.
Of 30 analysts tracked by TheStreet, 28 rate the stock a Buy, with an average target of $1,573, because they expect 2027 sales to roughly double to $275.3 billion.
TrendForce still expects DRAM, Micron's biggest product, to stay in short supply through 2027, which helps keep prices high.
bear: TrendForce lowered its 2027 forecasts after Chinese cloud companies cut memory orders, the kind of news that signals the price boom could end.
BNP Paribas warned memory demand could peak sooner than expected and lead to too much supply, which would push memory prices down.
US export rules bar Micron from selling its high-bandwidth AI memory to Chinese customers, shutting it out of a big market.

briefs.name: Micron Technology
briefs.whyMoved: Micron fell from $778.31 on November 13 to $594.51 on November 20, bounced, then dropped 4.5% to $601.25 on November 25 before jumping 7.60% to $646.95 on Friday, November 27, as chip stocks rebounded. The November 25 drop came after research firm TrendForce said Chinese cloud companies cut their 2027 memory orders and BNP Paribas warned memory demand could peak sooner than expected. This matters because Micron's profit comes from memory prices: last quarter it kept 87 cents of every sales dollar after making the chips, so even a small fall in prices cuts profit fast. NAND storage chips are about a quarter of Micron's sales, and TrendForce sees NAND prices entering a downward cycle.

watch.what: Some CHIPS Act limits end, letting Micron return more cash to owners; a large buyback plan would show management confidence.
Quarterly results; sales near $61.5 billion and a gross margin near 86% would match guidance, while weaker 2027 order comments would feed peak-demand fears.

briefs.headline: Domino's climbs to $358.30, up 4.9% in two weeks after a Baird upgrade
briefs.about: Domino's Pizza is the world's biggest pizza chain, with stores in over 90 countries. Most stores are owned by franchisees, who pay Domino's fees and buy dough and supplies from it.
briefs.whyMoved: Domino's rose from $341.72 on November 13 to $361.53 on November 25, then eased to $358.30 on November 27, a 4.9% gain over two weeks. The push started November 13, when Baird analyst Chris O'Cull raised the stock to Outperform with a $400 target, saying he sees a clearer path to better sales, especially bigger order sizes in the fourth quarter. Domino's earns most of its money from franchise fees and from selling dough and supplies to its stores, so it needs more pizzas sold at existing stores. That is the weak spot: US same-store sales (sales at stores open at least a year) grew just 0.3% last quarter, down from 5.2% a year earlier.
briefs.summary: Last quarter's profit was $4.60 per share, beating the $4.33 analysts expected, on sales of $1.19 billion, up 3.4%. Even after the rally, the stock is down about 19.7% in 2026. State Street cut its stake by 53.1% in the third quarter, while EVP Frank Garrido sold 2,850 shares at $348.52 on November 17. The quarterly dividend is $1.99 per share.
bull: Baird's $400 target is about 12% above the November 27 price, and its upgrade drove a 15.5% one-month rally.
Profit per share of $4.60 beat estimates and rose from $4.08 a year earlier, helped by wider margins and new stores around the world.
MarketBeat's analyst average target is $380.69, with 18 Buy-type ratings versus 1 Sell.
bear: US same-store sales grew only 0.3%, and the finance chief said full-year growth should land toward the low end of the plan.
Global retail sales grew 3.2% to $4.84 billion, about half the 6.3% growth a year earlier.
Baird warned weaker 2026 results could slow how many new stores open in 2027, and international same-store sales rose just 0.2%.

watch.what: Last day to be on record for the $1.99 per share dividend, a yield of about 2.2% a year.
Domino's pays the $1.99 dividend.

market.why: On Friday, November 27, stocks rose in a short Black Friday session that ended at 1 p.m., capping the S&P 500's best week since April 2025, up 5.6%. Beaten-down AI and chip stocks led the bounce, with Micron up 7.6% and AMD up 4.6%, which lifted the tech-heavy Nasdaq the most. Amazon rose about 4% on early holiday shopping news, helping the Dow gain 592 points, and the smaller companies in the Russell 2000 rose 1.7%, finishing up 6.5% for the week.
